mechanism_narrative: The observed steady recovery in RETAIL_REC over the past four weeks, moving from -46.0% to -40.6%, indicates a persistent underlying trend of increasing consumer activity, which will continue to drive further improvements in retail and recreation mobility over the next four weeks.
failure_condition: The mean RETAIL_REC over the next 28 days is lower than the mean RETAIL_REC over the last 28 days.

mechanism_narrative: The sharp decline in PARKS mobility from 49.0% to 27.3% in the most recent week was a temporary dip, likely due to transient factors. As conditions normalize, people will return to outdoor activities, leading to a rebound in PARKS and subsequently increased foot traffic to nearby retail and recreation establishments.
candidate_trigger: PARKS increases by more than 10 points week-on-week
failure_condition: PARKS mobility does not rebound significantly, and RETAIL_REC does not show an increase in the subsequent two weeks.

mechanism_narrative: Despite current low levels, any coordinated increase in both WORKPLACES and TRANSIT mobility would signal a significant return to office-based work and commuting, directly boosting weekday retail and recreation activity in commercial districts over the next four weeks.
candidate_trigger: WORKPLACES and TRANSIT both increase by > 5 points week-on-week
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC does not increase even if both WORKPLACES and TRANSIT show a sustained increase over two consecutive weeks.

mechanism_narrative: The stabilization of RESIDENTIAL mobility at elevated levels (around 13-15%) suggests that a significant portion of the population continues to spend more time at home. This sustained pattern will continue to suppress discretionary retail and recreation outings, preventing a substantial recovery over the next four weeks.
failure_condition: RESIDENTIAL mobility drops below 10% change from baseline for two consecutive weeks, and RETAIL_REC shows a strong upward trend.

mechanism_narrative: The recent decline in GROCERY_PHARM mobility from -19.4% to -20.4%, if it continues, indicates a broader reduction in essential outings, which often precedes or accompanies a reduction in discretionary retail and recreation activities due to increased caution or reduced overall movement.
candidate_trigger: GROCERY_PHARM falls by more than 2 points week-on-week
failure_condition: GROCERY_PHARM continues to decline, but RETAIL_REC shows an increase over the subsequent week.

mechanism_narrative: Despite a slight recent improvement, the overall RETAIL_REC levels remain significantly depressed (around -40%). Without a strong external catalyst, the momentum for recovery will stall, leading to continued low levels of retail and recreation mobility over the next four weeks.
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC shows an average increase of more than 5 points over the next four weeks compared to the last four weeks.

mechanism_narrative: If the recent dip in PARKS mobility (from 49.0% to 27.3%) is accompanied by a sustained increase in RESIDENTIAL mobility, it suggests a shift towards more home-bound leisure, reducing overall out-of-home activity including retail and recreation over the next two weeks.
candidate_trigger: PARKS falls by > 5 points and RESIDENTIAL rises by > 1 point week-on-week
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC increases over the next two weeks despite PARKS falling and RESIDENTIAL rising.

mechanism_narrative: The persistent stagnation of WORKPLACES mobility at severely reduced levels (around -46%) indicates that work-from-home policies remain dominant. This structural shift will continue to suppress weekday retail and recreation activity, preventing a significant recovery over the next four weeks.
failure_condition: WORKPLACES mobility increases by more than 10 points over the next four weeks, and RETAIL_REC also shows a significant increase.
